title: POC weekly sync - rollout & go-live planning
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on go-live cutover strategy: canary vs A/B, monitoring & runbooks, SLA expectations, security sign-offs. Agreed next steps include producing a canary checklist, setting up 1-week canary window, security docs handoff and a final cutover dry-run.
action_items: Priya Kapoor - create canary run checklist + monitoring playbook (include metrics, dashboards, alert thresholds) - due 2026-05-06
Jordan Meyers - share pricing delta for dedicated vs hosted during sustained canary traffic - due 2026-05-04
Kian Patel - provide expected request profile and top 10 prompt templates for canary traffic - due 2026-05-03
Renee Wu - confirm security requirements for key management (KMS/HSM) and any additional audit fields - due 2026-05-05
Liam Cho - schedule cutover dry-run for 2026-05-12 and invite stakeholders - due 2026-05-01
next_steps: Redwood to provision canary capacity and share runbook link (link: https://redwood.example/runbook/mosaic-canary)
Customer to share traffic sample and production-like dataset for monitoring baseline
Schedule dry-run cutover and confirm rollback criteria
Security team to review SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration notes
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-29 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45 min | Attendees: Jordan Meyers, Priya Kapoor, Liam Cho (Redwood) / Alex Torres, Sara Lim, Kian Patel, Renee Wu (Mosaic)

[00:00] Jordan: All right, kickin' off, thanks everyone for joining. Quick agenda — review last week's perf numbers, talk canary vs A/B approach for the cutover, monitoring & runbook, security sign-off, and next steps. Sound good?

[00:18] Alex: Yep, that works. We just want to make sure the cutover doesn't tank storefront latency during peak.

[00:25] Priya: Totally. I pulled the pod-level metrics and the tail latency looked stable in the 95th at about 220ms under the POC load, but that was with batching tuned down — remember we had to bias for latency.

[00:42] Kian: Right, for our user flows the median is fine but we care about 95/99. Also we saw a KV cache warm-up hit where cold starts spiked to ~1.3s a few times. Not sure if that's expected for our sequence lengths.

[01:05] Priya: That's expected on first prefix loads — Redwood's prefix/KV cache helps but you do see a warm-up window. For canary we recommend pre-warming with representative prompts, which is in the runbook.

[01:22] Sara: Quick question: are we leaning canary or A/B? Product thinks A/B would give us a safe rollback but ops prefers canary to limit blast radius.

[01:35] Jordan: Good point. Short answers: canary gives you graduated traffic and easier rollback, A/B gives clean percentage experiments and data for quality comparison. For a go-live I usually recommend a canary then a short A/B for quality checks, but depends on traffic patterns.

[01:55] Alex: Our traffic is spiky: weekdays noon and after 6pm. Can we ramp canary to 5% then 25 then 100 over X days automatically? What's the mechanism?

[02:12] Priya: We support policy-based routing. You can configure ramp windows — e.g., 5% for 24h, then 25% for 48h, then 100%. We also suggest failure thresholds — e.g., if 95th latency > 500ms or error rate > 0.5% for 15m, rollback automatically. Those are in the runbook template.

[02:37] Renee: From security: we need audit logs for every inference payload (redacted) and KMS key usage logs. Also SSO + RBAC mapping before production.

[02:50] Liam: Noted. We have the audit log pipeline and KMS integration examples — we'll send the SOC2 artifacts.

[03:00] Sara: Another operational ask: what about monitoring dashboards and alert pages? We need a single pane for model-level latency, cost per token, and fallback counts.

[03:15] Priya: We'll build a dashboard pre-populated with those panels — latency percentiles, token throughput, cost burn rate, cache hit ratio, and fallback events. We'll also add synthetic checks for cold start scenarios. Link in next steps.

[03:35] Kian: For the canary, we want to measure quality regressions — how do you suggest we do that? We have a test set of prompts but want real-time checks.

[03:47] Priya: Two options: online A/B with automatic evals on a sampled subset, or continuous offline evals using your prompt set and Redwood Evaluate. For real-time, sample 1% of traffic, run a lightweight reranker/eval and surface score deltas.

[04:10] Alex: Cost — running a canary on dedicated capacity worries finance. What's the delta vs hosted for this ramp?

[04:20] Jordan: There is a delta. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput but has a sustained cost commitment. For a short canary you could burst on hosted or use reserved burst capacity. I'll calculate the delta and send numbers — expecting about a 15-25% premium during the canary window if you choose dedicated-only.

[04:44] Sara: OK, that helps. Also we need a rollback playbook — criteria and operator steps. Please include automatic and manual rollback flows.

[04:55] Priya: Runbook will include both: automated policies keyed to SLOs and a manual operator checklist (traffic cut, DNS swap, config flags, notify downstream teams). We'll also include a dry-run checklist.

[05:10] Jordan: Let's talk timeline: customer wants production launch mid-May. That gives us two weeks for canary and one dry-run. Does that align?

[05:20] Alex: Mid-May is the target, yes. Two weeks for canary is acceptable if the ramp is gradual.

[05:28] Kian: We'll provide traffic samples and top prompts by end of this week. That should help pre-warm and set thresholds.

[05:36] Renee: Security will need the KMS integration docs and proof-of-concept for audit logs. If we get those this week we can sign off by 05-05.

[05:46] Liam: We'll push the SOC2 pack and the KMS notes after this call.

[05:54] Priya: One technical note — if you have vault HSM requirement, Redwood supports external KMS, and we'll show key rotation and envelope encryption in the runbook. There might be slight perf overhead for external KMS operations; we can quantify that in the dry-run.

[06:12] Alex: How about fallback models? If the primary model hits errors or latency we want immediate fallback to a smaller variant or older model. Can we do that automatically?

[06:23] Priya: Yes — we support model variant failover rules. You can define fallback chains: primary -> quantized smaller model -> cached responses. We'll show an example policy.

[06:36] Jordan: Also recommend traffic shaping for heavy prompt templates, e.g., lower batch size or different quant settings for long sequences. That's in the Optimize recommendations.

[06:47] Sara: For observability, can you provide token-level cost breakdowns per route? We want to tie spend to features.

[06:55] Priya: Yep, the console has per-route token cost and we can wire that to your billing export. We'll include a sample dashboard.

[07:05] Kian: About canary duration: do you have a recommended minimum observation window per ramp step?

[07:12] Priya: Recommend at least 24h at each lower percentage to capture traffic patterns; longer if your distributions are highly diurnal. For a two-week plan, 5% 48h, 25% 72h, then 100% after dry-run is a reasonable pattern.

[07:30] Jordan: Let's capture the rollback criteria now — 95th latency > 500ms for 15m, error rate > 0.5% for 15m, quality delta (BLEU-like or bespoke metric) drop > 5% on sampled eval. Any objections?

[07:46] Alex: Sounds good. We'll align on the metric definitions offline.

[07:52] Renee: Also note compliance: we need to retain audit logs for 1 year and have exportable CSVs for audits. Please include retention settings in the runbook.

[08:02] Priya: We'll add retention config and export steps.

[08:10] Sara: One more ops question: who is the primary on-call on Redwood side during the canary? We need a contact list.

[08:17] Liam: I'll be primary for the first week; Priya will be on-call for any infra incidents. We'll provide escalation matrix.

[08:25] Jordan: Okay, quick recap of next steps: Priya to deliver runbook and canary checklist, Jordan to send pricing delta, Kian to send traffic samples, Renee to confirm KMS bits. Schedule dry-run for 2026-05-12.

[08:38] Sara: Great. Anything else?

[08:42] Alex: No, that covers it. Thanks.

[08:46] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the runbook link and calendar invite.

[08:52] Meeting end.
